items.stem: A dataset is read a few times a year for audits and must be retained cheaply. Which storage class fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: Archive is the lowest-cost class for data accessed less than once a year.
Standard is for frequently accessed data and costs the most to store.
Nearline targets roughly monthly access, more frequent than this case.
Local SSD is instance storage, not an object storage class.

items.explanation: Correct: Archive is the cheapest class for rarely accessed, long-retained data.

items.stem: Which TWO give access to a single object without making a bucket public? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Generate a time-limited signed URL for the object
options.rationale: Correct: a signed URL grants scoped, temporary access to one object.

options.text: Grant a specific principal an IAM role on the object or bucket
options.rationale: Correct: IAM grants least-privilege access to named principals.

options.text: Set the bucket to allUsers with Storage Object Viewer
options.rationale: Granting allUsers makes the data public.

options.text: Disable public access prevention for the project
options.rationale: That weakens protection and does not scope access to one object.

items.explanation: Correct: signed URLs and targeted IAM grants both avoid making the bucket public.

items.stem: You want deleted objects to be recoverable. What must be enabled first?

options.rationale: Correct: versioning preserves noncurrent versions so deletes can be restored.
Storage class affects cost, not recoverability of deletes.
CMEK controls encryption, not delete recovery.
Website config is unrelated to object recovery.

items.explanation: Correct: object versioning is required to recover deleted objects.
